name: a_movers_session
prompt:
Search the web now. You are a financial fact extractor for a US-equity pre-market brief.
Brief date: Monday October 5, 2026. Topic: Session movers.

Window: Friday October 2, 2026 regular session (9:30-16:00 ET) through Monday October 5, 2026 12:20 ET, including after-hours, overnight and pre-market news. This spans 2 non-trading day(s): news published on those days (e.g. Saturday and Sunday) is in scope and often the most important. Anything published after 12:20 ET on Monday October 5, 2026 is out of scope.

FIND
US stocks >= $2B market cap making the biggest moves in the regular session (CNBC / MarketWatch / Barron's / Investopedia / Reuters mover roundups): % move and the stated catalyst for each.

Run multiple searches with different phrasings and dates. Prefer primary sources and wire services
(Reuters, Bloomberg, AP, CNBC, WSJ, MarketWatch, Barron's, Investopedia, company press releases, SEC
EDGAR, BLS/BEA/Census/Fed releases, FDA). For every item give the latest status as of the cutoff.

OUTPUT (markdown; no intro or conclusion). Group by ticker or topic:

## TICKER or Topic `[Category]`
- fact (source)

Category: pick from AI Compute · Memory & Interconnect · Optical & Photonics · Chip Equipment · Fab & Foundry · Wireless & Mobile · Analog & Mixed-Signal · Power & Wide-Bandgap · Test & Advanced Packaging · Specialty Materials & IP Licensing · Quantum Computing · EdgeAI · Semiconductors · AI Infrastructure · Software & SaaS · Internet & Platforms · Communications & Networking, or Macro / Commodities / Geopolitics / Crypto / Calendar /
Pharma / Energy / Retail, or a concise sector name. Bold tickers.

RULES
- Facts only. Every bullet has a specific number, name, or date. No bullet without a data point.
- End every bullet with the named source and publish time if known: (Reuters, Sep 24 07:12 ET).
  Convert every time to ET (ET = GMT-4 / UTC-4 in EDT; 09:59 GMT = 05:59 ET) before judging whether
  it is inside the window. For prices quoted several times, report the latest reading before the
  cutoff with its time.
  "Analysts said" / "reports suggest" without a name is not allowed.
- Earnings: actual vs consensus for EPS and revenue; guidance old → new.
- Analyst actions: firm, rating old → new, PT old → new.
- Mark unconfirmed items (people familiar, leaks, social media, M&A speculation) with [rumor]. A
  Bloomberg/Reuters/WSJ report citing sources is still reportable: state it and mark [report].
- If one event moved several stocks, name every stock and its move in the same bullet.
- Only facts published in the window. Older background only if it is the direct cause of a move in
  the window, labelled with its date.
- Do not interpret price action. Do not write "strong", "beat expectations", "investors cheered",
  "remains", "continues to", "well-positioned", "tailwinds". Write the number.
- Do not write bullets about what you could not find. Omit the topic instead.
- Do not drop facts to save space.
content:
## **TSLA** — Semiconductors / Automotive
- **Tesla** rose **4.7%** on Friday, October 2, after reporting **486,532 third-quarter vehicle deliveries**, above the **461,100 FactSet analyst estimate**. (CNBC, Oct. 2; publication time not shown)[2][10]
- Tesla’s shares were reported up **4.65%** in Friday’s regular session. (Investing.com, Oct. 5 09:43 ET)[15]

## **AVGO** — AI Compute
- **Broadcom** rose **more than 3%** on Friday after Reuters reported that Broadcom had agreed to lend **Anthropic up to $42 billion** to finance infrastructure purchases; separate reporting described **$42 billion of Class A senior secured debt** and **$18 billion of Class B debt**. (CNBC, Oct. 2; publication time not shown)[2]
- Broadcom rose approximately **3.5%** after Bloomberg reported that its syndicate was assembling **$60 billion of AI-chip financing** for Anthropic and other companies. (Yahoo Finance, Oct. 2; publication time not shown)[13]

## **NKE** — Retail
- **Nike** fell approximately **3.5%** in Friday’s regular session after fiscal-first-quarter revenue missed LSEG consensus, sales declined **4%**, China sales weakened, and the company announced planned staff reductions in **2027**. (Yahoo Finance, Oct. 2; publication time not shown)[10][13]
- CNBC reported that Nike shares fell nearly **6%** midday after the revenue miss and the company’s disclosure of a **4% sales decline** and planned **2027 layoffs**. (CNBC, Oct. 2; publication time not shown)[2]

## **ON** — Semiconductors
- **ON Semiconductor** rose more than **5%** Friday after revising its offer to acquire Synaptics to **$123 per share in cash**, valuing the transaction at approximately **$5.7 billion**, down from the prior **$7 billion** agreement. (CNBC, Oct. 2; publication time not shown)[2]
- ON Semiconductor rose approximately **7%** in premarket trading after reports of the revised acquisition offer. (CNBC, Oct. 2; publication time not shown)[4]

## **SYNA** — Semiconductors
- **Synaptics** rose approximately **14%** in Friday’s regular session after ON Semiconductor revised its acquisition offer to **$123 per share in cash**, valuing the transaction at **$5.7 billion**. (CNBC, Oct. 2; publication time not shown)[2]
- Synaptics rose more than **14%** premarket on the acquisition report. (CNBC, Oct. 2; publication time not shown)[4]

## **STX** — Memory & Interconnect
- **Seagate Technology** fell approximately **10.21%** Friday, with one market-mover report recording a decline of **11.61%**. (Investing.com, Oct. 5 09:43 ET)[15]
- Seagate shares fell more than **11%** premarket after a Nikkei report said Toshiba would **double hard-disk-drive production capacity** for data centers and invest **$380 million** to expand facilities in the Philippines. (CNBC, Oct. 2; publication time not shown)[4]

## **WDC** — Memory & Interconnect
- **Western Digital** fell approximately **8%** Friday after a Nikkei report said Toshiba would double hard-disk-drive production capacity for data centers and invest **$380 million** in Philippine facilities. (CNBC, Oct. 2; publication time not shown)[4]
- Western Digital was reported among the stocks that declined by double digits during Friday’s session, alongside Seagate. (Yahoo Finance, Oct. 2; publication time not shown)[13]

## **MXL** — Communications & Networking
- **MaxLinear** rose approximately **12.62%** Friday; the company was listed among the **$2 billion–$10 billion market-capitalization** movers. (Investing.com, Oct. 5 09:43 ET)[15]

## **TER** — Test & Advanced Packaging
- **Teradyne** rose approximately **5.79%** Friday and was listed among large-cap movers with market capitalization between **$10 billion and $200 billion**. (Investing.com, Oct. 5 09:43 ET)[15]

## **ONTO** — Chip Equipment
- **Onto Innovation** rose more than **5%** Friday after RBC Capital Markets initiated coverage with an **outperform** rating and a **$50 price target**, compared with Thursday’s close of **$36**, implying approximately **37% upside**. (CNBC, Oct. 2; publication time not shown)[2]

## **ARM** — AI Compute
- **Arm Holdings** rose approximately **7.24%** Friday in one market-mover report. (Investing.com, Oct. 5 09:43 ET)[15]

## **HPE** — AI Infrastructure
- **Hewlett Packard Enterprise** rose approximately **5.87%** Friday after Daiwa upgraded the stock on a networking-growth outlook. (Investing.com, Oct. 5 09:43 ET)[15]

## **VECO** — Chip Equipment
- **Veeco Instruments** rose approximately **8.46%** Friday and was listed among companies with market capitalizations between **$2 billion and $10 billion**. (Investing.com, Oct. 5 09:43 ET)[15]

## **IART** — Pharma
- **Integra LifeSciences** fell approximately **20.33%** Friday; a company update cited expected third-quarter revenue of approximately **$410 million to $412 million** and adjusted diluted EPS of **$0.55 to $0.59**, alongside the continuing impact of a **July flooding event** at its Cincinnati facility. (Stockmarketwatch.com, Oct. 3 05:18 ET; Yahoo Finance, Oct. 3; publication time not shown)[12][6]

## **EL** — Retail
- **Estée Lauder** rose **2.8%** on Monday, October 5, after Barclays upgraded the stock to **overweight** from **equal weight**. (CNBC, Oct. 5 11:50 ET)[1]

## Macro / Calendar
- The S&P 500, Dow Jones Industrial Average, and Nasdaq Composite rose approximately **0.7%**, **0.5%**, and **1.2%**, respectively, on Friday, October 2, after U.S. payrolls increased by **29,000** in the latest monthly report. (Yahoo Finance, Oct. 2; publication time not shown)[13]
- Monday’s scheduled U.S. releases included the final **S&P Global Composite PMI at 09:45 ET** and the **ISM Services PMI at 10:00 ET**. (CNBC, Oct. 4; last updated Oct. 5 09:31 ET)[3]
